payload.gap_claim: Scanned against the design document's own ladder and the alternatives it already eliminated. (1) ACTION BUTTONS ALONE, today's v2 rung: sheds the reasoning - two labels and no way to see what is being decided, so the owner either trusts blindly or waits until they are back at the desk. (2) A TUNNEL TO THE MACHINE (cloudflared, v1's original): sheds availability - it requires the home machine awake, and the design records it as fundamentally broken from a cloud sandbox anyway. (3) AN ARTIFACT PAGE (§11 rung 3): sheds the answer leg - its content-security policy blocks every outbound request, so it can display a brief but never carry the bless back. (4) PLAIN CHAT: sheds the away case entirely; it needs the harness. (5) ANONYMOUS PASTE HOSTS: shed rendering - the design records that anti-phishing economics force text/plain or a download, so an HTML brief never renders. THE CLAIM: only a statically-hosted, self-decrypting page LINKED FROM a card that also carries direct actions gets all four at once - reachable anywhere, readable on its merits, answerable in one tap, and opaque to the host.
payload.why_now: Three things are already true, which is why this is a port rather than an invention. The transport was built and verified end to end on 2026-07-21 - worker, namespace, token, publish, serve, notify, and a real phone tap in the UC-2 dry run - and this session re-verified both prerequisites: the token is present and the worker still serves. v1 has the shape in production form: one browsable page per bless moment, the same page travelling as the ask's link, with the actions and the page sharing one card. And the phone lane's other half now demonstrably works - the owner blessed i5d's release gate from their phone today, hash-bound, recorded channel=phone. What is missing is only the two legs between them.
payload.value_props:
PROP 1 - audience: the owner adjudicating away from the desk. Need|outcome: I can act on the notification I receive | a tap returns a grant. Alternative today: a button that errors with 'Expected URL scheme http or https'. Difference: the answer topic is absolutized against its base, exactly as v1 does. PASS LINE: a tap on a published card produces a recorded grant with channel=phone, demonstrated on a real device, not asserted.

PROP 2 - audience: the same owner, deciding rather than rubber-stamping. Need|outcome: I can see what I am blessing | the card links a page carrying the gate's brief and its evidence. Alternative today: 400 characters of truncated message. Difference: one self-contained page per bless moment. PASS LINE: the page opens on the phone and shows the gate's evidence fields, and the card's title marks it as a GATE rather than a question.

PROP 3 - audience: the owner as the person whose material it is. Need|outcome: the host cannot read my decisions | the page is published encrypted with its key only in the URL fragment. PASS LINE: fetching the published key without the fragment returns ciphertext that contains none of the brief's words.

PROP 4 - audience: the agent, and the owner who must trust it unattended. Need|outcome: a lane that is not working says so | every publish records success or failure where both can see it. Alternative today: silence. PASS LINE: an induced publish failure appears in the record, and the gate still goes out with its action buttons rather than vanishing.

PROP 5 - audience: the agent choosing a mode. Need|outcome: a gate the owner must bless always reaches the phone | the publish is driven by who adjudicates, not by whether a process happens to be up. PASS LINE: a human-blessed gate publishes even when the lane's configuration changed after the board started.
payload.business_case: Skipped with reason: no acquirer - internal tooling, and the currency is the owner's own availability. The measurable return is stated in the pass lines: the difference between an iteration that waits for the owner to come back to the machine and one they can close from a train.
